title: Rongzai agent: A Large Language Model-Based Autonomous Assistant for Rietveld Refinement of Neutron Diffraction Data
summary: Neutron diffraction (ND) is an indispensable technique for determining atomic positions (especially light elements) and thus serves as a critical probe for revealing microscopic structures in materials science. However, traditional Rietveld refinement of ND data relies heavily on manual operation of specialized software, which is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and highly dependent on user expertise, severely hindering automated analysis. The automation of Rietveld refinement has long been a long-standing and challenging problem in crystallography. To address this challenge, this paper presents the Dr.Sai-Rongzai agent, an autonomous refinement assistant based on a large language model (LLM), a specialist knowledge base, and the GSAS-II refinement engine, achieving for the first time an intelligent refinement that integrates knowledge-driven decision-making. The agent accomplishes a fully automated workflow from natural language task parsing to autonomous decision-making, execution of refinement strategies, and report generation. Evaluation on five representative samples shows that the Rongzai agent achieves lower Rwp values than human specialists on three samples (2.88% vs. 4.42%, 5.06% vs. 5.40%, 7.60% vs. 9.00%), while on the other two samples its results are very close to those of the specialists. The agent is currently deployed at the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) and is open for external user registration, providing an intelligent and user-friendly analytical tool for materials research. This work fully leverages the cutting-edge advantages of LLM, offers a new path to solve the long-standing problem of automated refinement, takes a key step toward intelligent and fully automated crystallographic analysis, and holds great potential to accelerate AI for Science discoveries in neutron-based materials characterization.

AI.tldr: Dr.Sai-Rongzai is an LLM-based autonomous agent that automates Rietveld refinement of neutron diffraction data, outperforming or matching human specialists across five samples, and is deployed at CSNS.
AI.motivation: Traditional Rietveld refinement of neutron diffraction data is manual, time-consuming, labor-intensive, and expertise-dependent, creating a long-standing bottleneck in automated crystallographic analysis.
AI.method: The agent integrates a large language model (LLM), a specialist knowledge base, and the GSAS-II refinement engine to enable an autonomous workflow from natural language task parsing to strategy execution and report generation.
AI.result: On five representative samples, the agent achieved lower Rwp values than human specialists on three samples (2.88% vs. 4.42%, 5.06% vs. 5.40%, 7.60% vs. 9.00%) and comparable results on the other two. Deployed at CSNS and open for external registration.
AI.conclusion: This work demonstrates that LLM-driven automation can solve the long-standing problem of automated Rietveld refinement, enabling intelligent crystallographic analysis and advancing AI for Science in neutron-based materials characterization.

title: Circularity in Perovskite-Based Tandem Photovoltaics for Terawatt-Scale Deployment
summary: As photovoltaics (PVs) scale from one to multiple terawatts over the next decade, ensuring sustainable deployment is urgently required. Crystalline silicon (c-Si) PVs, the current industry standard, will generate an estimated 160 million tonnes of waste by 2050, and there remains complex technoeconomic challenges associated with their recycling. Metal-halide perovskite (MHP)-based tandem PVs not only promise higher power conversion efficiencies than single-junction c-Si devices, but also offer intrinsic advantages for circularity, including simpler device architectures, low-temperature processing, and more accessible materials recovery routes. At this pivotal juncture when perovskite PVs begin to enter the market, this review examines the critical circularity challenges that must be addressed: substitution of scarce raw materials, scalable recycling protocols, cost-effective stack delamination, safe lead sequestration, and policy frameworks to encourage circularity across the device lifecycle with effective incentives. By integrating the materials, technoeconomic and policy dimensions that go beyond conventional lifecycle assessments, we outline actionable strategies to co-optimize device performance and sustainability. This review aims to guide researchers, policymakers, and industry stakeholders in steering perovskite-based tandem PVs towards a circular and responsible commercialization pathway within the global clean-energy transition.

AI.tldr: This review examines circularity challenges for perovskite-based tandem photovoltaics, including scarce material substitution, scalable recycling, lead sequestration, and policy frameworks, arguing they offer intrinsic sustainability advantages over crystalline silicon PVs.
AI.motivation: As c-Si PVs scale to multiple terawatts and are projected to generate 160 million tonnes of waste by 2050 with complex recycling challenges, there is an urgent need for more sustainable photovoltaic technologies. Perovskite-based tandems promise higher efficiency and better circularity, but their commercialization requires proactive examination of sustainability pathways.
AI.method: The paper is a review integrating materials science, technoeconomic analysis, and policy dimensions beyond conventional lifecycle assessments to identify critical circularity challenges and outline actionable strategies.
AI.result: Identifies five critical circularity challenges: substitution of scarce raw materials, scalable recycling protocols, cost-effective stack delamination, safe lead sequestration, and policy frameworks for device lifecycle incentives.
AI.conclusion: Perovskite-based tandem PVs present intrinsic circularity advantages over c-Si, but achieving sustainable commercialization requires co-optimizing device performance and sustainability through integrated materials, technoeconomic, and policy strategies.

title: A Neural-Network Framework to Learn History-Dependent Constitutive Laws and Identifiability of Internal Variables
summary: The identification of constitutive laws is ubiquitous in engineering: in modeling of materials where experimental data are fitted to mathematical models or learning surrogate models to beat the FE\textsuperscript{2} computational cost of multiscale numerical simulations. However, these models of constitutive laws, unless equipped with a potential formulation, are not necessarily consistent with (a) the second law of thermodynamics; (b) stability of the material under extreme applied strain; and (c) the mathematical theory underpinning the existence of solutions of the governing equation. In this work, we present a causal and energetic formulation, consistent with aforementioned properties, of learning a history-dependent constitutive law. This characterization of the class of internal variables sheds light on the equivalence class of equivalent surrogate models for the constitutive law. We show that the internal variables that are learned from the data are unique up to a linear transform. The framework is deployed to learn the Taylor-averaged response of a polycrystalline magnesium unit cell. We achieve 2\% relative error in the prediction of the Taylor-averaged response.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a causal and energetic formulation for learning history-dependent constitutive laws that guarantees thermodynamic consistency, material stability, and mathematical well-posedness, achieving 2% relative error in predicting the Taylor-averaged response of polycrystalline magnesium.
AI.motivation: To address the lack of thermodynamic consistency, material stability, and mathematical well-posedness in standard data-driven constitutive law learning (e.g., surrogate models for FE²), ensuring the learned models respect fundamental physical principles.
AI.method: A causal and energetic formulation of learning history-dependent constitutive laws, with internal variables characterized by an equivalence class unique up to a linear transform, deployed to learn the Taylor-averaged response of a polycrystalline magnesium unit cell.
AI.result: Achieved 2% relative error in the prediction of the Taylor-averaged response of the polycrystalline magnesium unit cell.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides thermodynamically consistent, stable, and mathematically well-posed surrogate constitutive models, with internal variable uniqueness up to linear transform.

title: Carrier-density dependence of magnetotransport in correlated Dirac semimetal CaIrO$_3$
summary: We report the carrier density dependence of the magnetotransport property in the correlated Dirac semimetal CaIrO$_3$. In the dilute carrier density region ($n_{\rm H}$ $\sim 2.2 \times 10^{16} \,$$\rm{cm}^{-3}$) at $2 \, \mathrm{K}$, the mobility exceeds $1.0 \times 10^{5} \,$$\rm{cm}^{2}/\rm{Vs}$ at $2 \, \mathrm{K}$, and the transverse magnetoresistance (MR) reaches $2,000 \,$\% at $12 \, \mathrm{T}$. The analysis of quantum oscillations and Hall conductivity shows that the Fermi velocity is nearly independent of the cross-sectional area of the Fermi surface, or equivalently the carrier density, supporting a $k$-linear dispersion of the Dirac node. The field dependence of magnetoresistivity is nearly $B$-linear in the moderate carrier density region ($n_\mathrm{H} \geq 4 \times 10^{16}\,$cm$^{-3}$), but scales with $B^α$ ($α> 2$) in the lower carrier density region. The variation of magnetoresistivity is likely affected by the enhanced long-range Coulomb interaction in the quantum limit, where Dirac electrons are subject to the magnetic confinement.

AI.tldr: The study investigates magnetotransport in the correlated Dirac semimetal CaIrO₃, revealing ultrahigh mobility (>1.0×10⁵ cm²/Vs) and giant magnetoresistance (2,000% at 12 T) at low carrier density (~2.2×10¹⁶ cm⁻³). Fermi velocity is carrier-density-independent, confirming linear Dirac dispersion. MR transitions from B-linear to superlinear (B^α, α>2) at lower densities, attributed to enhanced Coulomb interaction in the quantum limit.
AI.motivation: To understand how carrier density affects magnetotransport properties in correlated Dirac semimetals, particularly the role of Coulomb interactions in the quantum limit.
AI.method: Magnetotransport measurements, quantum oscillation analysis, and Hall conductivity measurements on CaIrO₃ single crystals across varying carrier densities.
AI.result: Mobility exceeds 1.0×10⁵ cm²/Vs at 2 K; transverse MR reaches 2,000% at 12 T; Fermi velocity is independent of carrier density (confirming linear Dirac dispersion); MR transitions from B-linear to B^α (α>2) scaling at low carrier density.
AI.conclusion: The field-dependent MR behavior change at low carrier density is likely due to enhanced long-range Coulomb interactions in the quantum limit under magnetic confinement.

title: Machine-learning-identified two-dimensional van der Waals multiferroics for four-state nonvolatile memory
summary: Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) multiferroics offer an attractive platform for four-state nonvolatile memory by combining switchable ferroelectric polarization and magnetization within a single material system. However, their development is hindered by the scarcity of synthesizable candidates and the lack of non-destructive readout schemes. Here, we combine machine-learning screening with first-principles calculations to explore the 2D vdW ABC$_2$X$_6$ family and identify a set of high-confidence multiferroic candidates. Among them, AuCrP$_2$S$_6$ monolayer emerges as a representative system with a ferromagnetic ground state, a sizable out-of-plane polarization of 7.46 pC/m, and a moderate ferroelectric switching barrier of $\sim$130 meV/f.u. Moreover, the nonlinear optical response mediated by the bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) in AuCrP$_2$S$_6$ provides a dual-channel probe of the ferroic orders, in which the polarization direction governs the photocurrent sign while the magnetic order selects the spin channel via robust exchange splitting. This intrinsic coupling enables the non-destructive readout of four logic states within a single atomic layer, thereby providing a practical blueprint for next-generation multistate optoelectronic memory.

AI.tldr: This paper uses machine-learning screening and first-principles calculations to identify 2D vdW multiferroic candidates in the ABC₂X₆ family, with AuCrP₂S₆ monolayer showing combined ferromagnetism and ferroelectricity, and its bulk photovoltaic effect enables non-destructive four-state readout for next-generation optoelectronic memory.
AI.motivation: The scarcity of synthesizable 2D vdW multiferroic candidates and the lack of non-destructive readout schemes hinder the development of four-state nonvolatile memory devices.
AI.method: Combined machine-learning screening with first-principles calculations to explore the 2D vdW ABC₂X₆ family, identifying high-confidence multiferroic candidates and analyzing their electronic, ferroelectric, and magneto-optical properties.
AI.result: AuCrP₂S₆ monolayer exhibits a ferromagnetic ground state, out-of-plane polarization of 7.46 pC/m, and a ferroelectric switching barrier of ~130 meV/f.u., with BPVE-mediated dual-channel optical readout of both ferroelectric and magnetic orders.
AI.conclusion: The intrinsic coupling between ferroic orders and nonlinear optical response enables non-destructive four-state readout in a single atomic layer, providing a practical blueprint for next-generation multistate optoelectronic memory.

title: Unified definition of ferroelectricity
summary: Recent theoretical and experimental advances in quantum ferroelectrics suggest that ferroelectricity can also emerge in non-polar space group, highlighting the limitations of conventional polar space group criteria in identifying ferroelectric materials. Here, we introduce a unified definition based on switchable polarization differences between energetically equivalent states, which naturally encompasses conventional and quantum ferroelectrics. Guided by this principle, we implement a high-throughput screening strategy that systematically identifies both conventional and quantum ferroelectrics among experimentally synthesized materials. In particular, we identify a new type of quantum ferroelectric in which the quantized polarization arises from arbitrary ionic displacements, in contrast to previous quantum ferroelectrics (including both fractional and integer quantum ferroelectrics) where quantized polarization results from fractional or integer ionic displacements. Notably, we find that materials such as Ba3I6 and Cs2PdC2 exhibit low switching barriers and robust insulating behavior, highlighting their experimental viability. Our results reconcile conventional and quantum ferroelectrics, expand the accessible materials landscape, and provide a practical roadmap for discovering next-generation ferroelectrics with advanced switchable functionalities.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a unified definition of ferroelectricity based on switchable polarization differences between energetically equivalent states, enabling high-throughput screening of both conventional and quantum ferroelectrics. It identifies a new type of quantum ferroelectric with quantized polarization from arbitrary ionic displacements, and highlights Ba3I6 and Cs2PdC2 as experimentally viable candidates.
AI.motivation: Recent advances show ferroelectricity can emerge in non-polar space groups, exposing the limitations of conventional polar space group criteria for identifying ferroelectrics. The authors aim to provide a unified framework that encompasses both conventional and quantum ferroelectrics.
AI.method: The authors propose a unified definition based on switchable polarization differences between energetically equivalent states. They implement a high-throughput screening strategy to systematically identify conventional and quantum ferroelectrics among experimentally synthesized materials.
AI.result: Identified a new type of quantum ferroelectric where quantized polarization arises from arbitrary ionic displacements (distinct from previous fractional/integer quantum ferroelectrics). Ba3I6 and Cs2PdC2 exhibit low switching barriers and robust insulating behavior, confirming experimental viability.
AI.conclusion: The unified definition reconciles conventional and quantum ferroelectrics, expands the accessible materials landscape, and provides a practical roadmap for discovering next-generation ferroelectrics with advanced switchable functionalities.

title: Depletion-mode N-polar AlN-based high electron mobility transistors with improved on/off ratios
summary: We report N-polar AlN-based high-electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) with a GaN channel thickness of 5.2 nm on N-polar AlN on sapphire. The threshold voltage is around -2.4 to -3.0 V with saturation currents over 240 mA/mm and on/off ratios as high as 10,000, much higher than previously reported N-polar AlN-based HEMTs. The high on/off ratio is attributed to the use of an abrupt AlN/GaN heterostructure with a dedicated AlN transition layer, together with improved gate leakage. The high frequency properties as well as the on-resistance of ~20 Ohm mm are all limited by the 2000 Ohm/square sheet resistance of the channel layer.

AI.tldr: The paper presents N-polar AlN/GaN HEMTs with a 5.2 nm GaN channel on sapphire, achieving a record on/off ratio of 10,000, saturation currents over 240 mA/mm, and a threshold voltage of -2.4 to -3.0 V. The improved performance is attributed to an abrupt AlN/GaN heterostructure with a dedicated AlN transition layer and reduced gate leakage, though further performance is limited by a high sheet resistance of 2000 Ohm/sq.
AI.motivation: To improve the performance of N-polar AlN-based HEMTs, which previously suffered from low on/off ratios and relatively poor electrical characteristics compared to other III-nitride HEMT technologies.
AI.method: Fabrication of N-polar AlN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire using a 5.2 nm GaN channel layer with an abrupt AlN/GaN heterostructure and a dedicated AlN transition layer.
AI.result: Threshold voltage of -2.4 to -3.0 V, saturation currents >240 mA/mm, on/off ratio up to 10,000, on-resistance ~20 Ohm·mm, and sheet resistance of 2000 Ohm/sq limiting high-frequency performance.
AI.conclusion: The abrupt AlN/GaN heterostructure with an AlN transition layer significantly improves the on/off ratio and overall device performance, but the high sheet resistance of the channel layer remains a limiting factor for on-resistance and high-frequency operation.

title: Ward identities and orbital magnetization in current density functional theory
summary: We revisit the derivation of the orbital magnetization formula for periodic crystals in current density functional theory (CDFT)[1]. Our new derivation computes the linear response of the energy density to a periodic magnetic field in the long-wavelength limit. We unveil a Ward identity which connects the current vertex to the derivative of the Kohn-Sham self-energy. The result of Ref.[1] is confirmed: the orbital magnetization of the interacting solid can be computed exactly (in principle) from the self-consistent eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of the Kohn-Sham equation of CDFT.

AI.tldr: The paper rederives the orbital magnetization formula for periodic crystals in current density functional theory (CDFT), confirming that the orbital magnetization of interacting solids can be computed from Kohn-Sham eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of CDFT.
AI.motivation: To revisit and provide a new derivation of the orbital magnetization formula for periodic crystals within CDFT, validating the previous result from Ref. [1].
AI.method: A new derivation that computes the linear response of the energy density to a periodic magnetic field in the long-wavelength limit, revealing a Ward identity connecting the current vertex to the derivative of the Kohn-Sham self-energy.
AI.result: Confirms the result of Ref. [1]: the orbital magnetization of interacting solids can be computed exactly (in principle) from the self-consistent eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of the CDFT Kohn-Sham equation.
AI.conclusion: The orbital magnetization formula derived in CDFT is validated through a new approach involving a Ward identity, reinforcing the theoretical foundation for computing magnetization in interacting periodic crystals.

title: Chiroptical Ternary Entropy Harvesting from Self-Assembled Block Copolymer Nanopatterns
summary: Nanoscale fabrication inevitably produces local stochasticity that is commonly treated as a defect, but can instead be harnessed as a material resource for information security. Here we report a chiroptical platform for ternary entropy harvesting based on stochastic Au nanopatterns formed by block copolymer self-assembly. By transducing fabrication-induced stochastic microstates into handedness-dependent optical responses through chiroptical mapping, our platform enables native ternary digitization rather than conventional binary encoding, allowing physically harvested ternary random sequences to be used for key generation. This raises the information density to log2(3) = 1.585 bits per trit, approximately 58.5% higher than the binary limit, enabling more entropy to be harvested from a limited physical footprint. The harvested outputs exhibit near-balanced symbol populations, negligible spatial and inter-sample correlations, Shannon entropy approaching the ternary ideal, and resistance to statistical and machine-learning-based prediction. These results establish self-assembled chiroptical nanostructures as a scalable platform for cryptographic key generation, secure edge devices, and distributed Internet-of-Things platforms.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a chiroptical platform that harnesses stochasticity from nanoscale fabrication (block copolymer self-assembled Au nanopatterns) to harvest ternary entropy for cryptographic key generation, achieving 1.585 bits per trit—58.5% higher than binary encoding—with near-ideal randomness and resistance to prediction attacks.
AI.motivation: To transform the inherent stochasticity of nanoscale fabrication from a defect into a useful resource for information security, overcoming the binary entropy limit to achieve higher information density from limited physical footprints.
AI.method: Block copolymer self-assembly was used to fabricate stochastic Au nanopatterns with chiroptical properties. The handedness-dependent optical responses transduce fabrication-induced stochastic microstates into ternary digitization (rather than binary), enabling physical harvesting of ternary random sequences for key generation.
AI.result: The platform achieved 1.585 bits per trit (58.5% higher than binary limit), nearly balanced symbol populations, negligible spatial and inter-sample correlations, Shannon entropy near the ternary ideal, and resistance to both statistical and machine-learning-based prediction attacks.
AI.conclusion: Self-assembled chiroptical nanostructures are established as a scalable platform for cryptographic key generation, secure edge devices, and distributed IoT applications, demonstrating that fabrication stochasticity can be intentionally harvested as an entropy source.

title: From spin splitting to projected mass in altermagnetic Chern matter
summary: Altermagnetic spin splitting alone does not define Chern matter. The relevant object is the exchange mass projected onto Hall-active surface, valley, orbital or interface sectors. We formulate this projected-mass criterion for compensated magnetic topology. The resulting two-channel $(C,\mathcal{A})$ diagnostic separates hidden compensated Hall responses from additive altermagnetic quantum anomalous Hall phases in a global insulating gap. It also guides interface, thickness and materials design strategies.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a projected-mass criterion to distinguish hidden compensated Hall responses from altermagnetic quantum anomalous Hall phases, introducing a two-channel (C, 𝒜) diagnostic for compensated magnetic topology.
AI.motivation: Altermagnetic spin splitting alone does not define Chern matter; a more precise criterion is needed to identify topologically nontrivial phases in compensated magnetic systems.
AI.method: The authors formulate a projected-mass criterion focusing on the exchange mass projected onto Hall-active sectors (surface, valley, orbital, interface). They develop a two-channel (C, 𝒜) diagnostic to separate hidden compensated Hall responses from additive altermagnetic quantum anomalous Hall phases.
AI.result: The two-channel (C, 𝒜) diagnostic effectively separates hidden compensated Hall responses from additive altermagnetic quantum anomalous Hall phases within a global insulating gap.
AI.conclusion: The criterion guides interface, thickness, and materials design strategies for realizing compensated magnetic topology.

title: Strain-Enhanced Hydrogen Evolution, Electrical, Optical, and Thermoelectric Properties of the Multifunctional 2D CrSi2N4 Monolayer
summary: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) is employed to evaluate the structural, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and electrocatalytic properties of monolayer CrSi2N4. Its symmetric N-Si-N-Cr-N-Si-N septuple-layer structure exhibits dynamic, thermal (300 K), and mechanical stability, supported by a -8.76 eV/atom cohesive energy. PBE and HSE06 functionals reveal an indirect bandgap of 0.58 eV and 2.16 eV, respectively, driven by localized Cr-3d and N-2p states. The monolayer features 15.57 static dielectric constant and maximum absorption coefficients of 0.9 X 10^6 cm-1 (visible) and 1.4 X 10^6 cm-1 (deep-UV). Semiclassical Boltzmann calculations predict an outstanding room-temperature n-type thermoelectric power factor of 3.5 x mW/mK2. For hydrogen evolution (HER), the basal plane yields a baseline hydrogen adsorption free energy (ΔGH) of 1.05 eV at the N-site. Applying +5% expansive biaxial strain improves HER kinetics, reducing ΔGH to 0.46 eV. Thus, CrSi2N4 is a resilient, tuneable candidate for waste-heat recovery, photodetectors, and sustainable electrocatalysis.

AI.tldr: First-principles DFT reveals that monolayer CrSi2N4 is a dynamically, thermally, and mechanically stable septuple-layer material with an indirect bandgap (0.58–2.16 eV), strong visible/UV absorption, excellent n-type thermoelectric power factor (3.5 mW/mK²), and HER activity improvable via biaxial strain (ΔGH from 1.05 to 0.46 eV).
AI.motivation: To evaluate the structural, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and electrocatalytic properties of monolayer CrSi2N4 using first-principles DFT, assessing its potential for waste-heat recovery, photodetectors, and sustainable electrocatalysis.
AI.method: First-principles DFT with PBE and HSE06 functionals for electronic structure; semiclassical Boltzmann transport for thermoelectric properties; hydrogen adsorption free energy calculations for HER activity under biaxial strain.
AI.result: Indirect bandgap of 0.58 eV (PBE) and 2.16 eV (HSE06); static dielectric constant 15.57; max absorption 0.9×10⁶ cm⁻¹ (visible) and 1.4×10⁶ cm⁻¹ (deep-UV); n-type power factor 3.5 mW/mK² at room temperature; baseline ΔGH = 1.05 eV at N-site, reduced to 0.46 eV under +5% biaxial strain.
AI.conclusion: CrSi2N4 is a resilient, tuneable candidate for waste-heat recovery, photodetectors, and sustainable electrocatalysis.

title: Shaping Maximally Localized Wannier Functions via Discrete Adiabatic Transport
summary: Maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs) are conventionally constructed by iteratively minimizing a spread functional over a high-dimensional gauge landscape. In this work, we present a non-variational constructive algorithm that unifies gauge smoothing and the eigenvalue problem of the projected position operator into a single deterministic framework. We demonstrate that discrete adiabatic transport across band degeneracies emerges naturally as an integral part of the solution procedure for the position eigenvectors. In this transport-aligned gauge, the Bloch overlaps exhibit an approximately linear phase dependence, allowing the Wannier centers to be extracted via deterministic fixed-point iterations and self-consistent updates rather than spread-functional minimization. Benchmark calculations for one- and two-dimensional systems yield spreads and orbital shapes in good agreement with standard minimization schemes. Furthermore, this analytical approach transparently isolates the physical origin of the $\mathcal{O}(L)$ mesh-dependent spread scaling ($L$ being the boundary seam resolution) observed in graphene, demonstrating that it is an intrinsic geometric manifestation of non-commuting projected position operators forcing finite gauge defects to accumulate along a one-dimensional boundary seam.

AI.tldr: A non-variational constructive algorithm for generating maximally localized Wannier functions is proposed, replacing iterative spread-functional minimization with a deterministic framework based on discrete adiabatic transport and fixed-point iterations. It naturally explains the O(L) mesh-dependent spread scaling in graphene as a geometric consequence of non-commuting projected position operators.
AI.motivation: Conventional MLWF construction relies on iterative minimization of a spread functional over a high-dimensional gauge landscape, which can be computationally expensive and lacks transparency in isolating the physical origin of spread behavior.
AI.method: The authors develop a non-variational constructive algorithm that unifies gauge smoothing with the eigenvalue problem of the projected position operator. The method uses discrete adiabatic transport across band degeneracies to determine the gauge, extracts Wannier centers via deterministic fixed-point iterations and self-consistent updates, and analyzes the projected position operator's non-commutativity to explain spread scaling.
AI.result: Benchmark calculations for 1D and 2D systems yield spreads and orbital shapes consistent with standard minimization schemes. The method transparently shows that the O(L) mesh-dependent spread scaling in graphene arises from non-commuting projected position operators forcing gauge defects to accumulate along a one-dimensional boundary seam.
AI.conclusion: The proposed deterministic approach offers an alternative to variational MLWF construction, providing both computational efficiency and deeper physical insight into the geometric origins of spread behavior in systems with band degeneracies.

title: Accurate computation of the electron-phonon interaction contribution to the total energy
summary: The standard Hamiltonian of a coupled electron-phonon system is based on second-order perturbation theory. The EPI contribution in the standard Hamiltonian consists of two terms, the EPI contribution to the band-structure energy and the partial-Fan-Migdal (FM)-occupied contribution. Within the non-adiabatic approximation, we derive a new expression for the partial-FM-occ contribution and show that it has the structure of a higher-order term, and not a second-order term. Along similar lines, we derive new expressions for the computation of the partial-FM-occ term. The new expressions for the partial-FM-occ term must be preferred over the standard expressions, in theoretical and computational studies, because they incorporate the complete physics underlying this term. Unlike the EPI contribution to individual eigenstates, the EPI contribution to the total energy must be computed in the non-adiabatic approximation for all materials, Infra-red (IR) active and IR-inactive. We report the computation of the standard Hamiltonian, for the first time, for Carbon polymorphs (diamond and hexagonal lonsdaleite) by including the EPI contribution to the total energy. This is the most accurate ab initio total energy reported till date. The present work also opens the way to compute the ab initio free-energy more accurately at finite temperatures by including the EPI contribution.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the standard partial-Fan-Migdal-occupied term in the electron-phonon interaction Hamiltonian is actually a higher-order term, not second-order, and derives new, more physically complete expressions. It also reports the first computation of the standard Hamiltonian including EPI contribution to total energy for carbon polymorphs (diamond and lonsdaleite), achieving the most accurate ab initio total energy to date.
AI.motivation: The standard Hamiltonian for coupled electron-phonon systems is based on second-order perturbation theory, but the true physical nature of the partial-FM-occ contribution was not correctly classified, leading to incomplete physics in theoretical and computational studies.
AI.method: The authors derive new expressions for the partial-FM-occ term within the non-adiabatic approximation, showing it has a higher-order structure rather than second-order. They also compute the standard Hamiltonian including EPI contribution to total energy for carbon polymorphs (diamond and lonsdaleite).
AI.result: The partial-FM-occ term is a higher-order term, not second-order. New expressions incorporating complete physics are derived. First-ever computation of the standard Hamiltonian including EPI total energy contribution for diamond and lonsdaleite yields the most accurate ab initio total energy reported to date.
AI.conclusion: The new expressions for the partial-FM-occ term must be preferred over standard ones. EPI contribution to total energy requires non-adiabatic approximation for all materials (IR active and inactive). This work enables more accurate ab initio free-energy calculations at finite temperatures.

title: Probing the Chirality of Trigonal Selenium and Tellurium by Spin and Orbital Hall Effects
summary: Chiral crystals exhibit enantiomer-dependent transport phenomena that generate pure spin or orbital currents, while the handedness sensitivity of spin and orbital Hall conductivities (SHC/OHC) remains insufficiently understood. Using first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that trigonal selenium and tellurium -- prototypical chiral semiconductors -- exhibit opposite signs of the SHC/OHC tensor elements $σ_{yx}^{S_y}$ and $σ_{yx}^{L_y}$ between their left- and right-handed enantiomers. This behavior originates from the mirror operation relating the two structures, described by space groups $P3_221$ (left-handed) and $P3_121$ (right-handed). Although both enantiomers share identical band structures and four nonzero SHC/OHC tensor components, $σ_{yx}^{S_y}$ and $σ_{yx}^{L_y}$ reverse sign due to the antisymmetric transformation of the spin/orbital Berry curvature under the $M_{xy}$ mirror operation. More generally, for mirror-related enantiomorphic structures, selected SHC/OHC tensor components can exhibit symmetry-governed sign reversal. For trigonal Se and Te, the calculated signs of these components can be directly correlated with the left- and right-handed structures under the chosen coordinate convention. These results clarify the symmetry origin of handedness-dependent SHC/OHC and suggest a possible route for correlating measurable SHC/OHC signals with structural handedness in specific chiral materials.

AI.tldr: This paper uses first-principles calculations to show that trigonal selenium and tellurium exhibit opposite signs of spin and orbital Hall conductivity tensor elements between left- and right-handed enantiomers, originating from the antisymmetric transformation of spin/orbital Berry curvature under mirror operations, establishing a symmetry-governed link between structural handedness and Hall conductivity sign.
AI.motivation: The handedness sensitivity of spin and orbital Hall conductivities (SHC/OHC) in chiral crystals remains insufficiently understood, despite known enantiomer-dependent transport phenomena generating pure spin or orbital currents.
AI.method: First-principles calculations on trigonal selenium and tellurium (chiral semiconductors with space groups P3_221 and P3_121), analyzing SHC/OHC tensor components and Berry curvature transformations under mirror operations.
AI.result: Left- and right-handed enantiomers of trigonal Se and Te show opposite signs of σ_{yx}^{S_y} and σ_{yx}^{L_y} tensor elements while sharing identical band structures and four nonzero SHC/OHC components, with sign reversal caused by antisymmetric transformation of spin/orbital Berry curvature under M_{xy} mirror operation.
AI.conclusion: Symmetry origin of handedness-dependent SHC/OHC is clarified, suggesting a possible route for correlating measurable SHC/OHC signals with structural handedness in chiral materials.

title: Methane hydrate nucleation frustration and dimensional reduction of structural order under nanoconfinement
summary: Methane hydrate nucleation under nanoconfinement remains poorly understood due to the complex interplay between geometric restriction and molecular ordering. Here, we investigate the structural organization of water-methane systems confined between silica planar slit pores with widths ranging from 1 to 5 nm and temperatures between 250 and 295 K. Three-dimensional radial distribution functions reveal a clear suppression of hydrate-like ordering at strong confinement (below 2 nm), indicating frustrated nucleation. In contrast, projected two-dimensional correlations exhibit pronounced in-plane structural organization, evidencing a confinement-induced reduction in the dimensionality of molecular order.

AI.tldr: This study investigates methane hydrate nucleation under nanoconfinement in silica slit pores (1–5 nm width, 250–295 K), finding that strong confinement below 2 nm suppresses hydrate-like ordering due to frustrated nucleation, while in-plane structural organization emerges from reduced dimensionality.
AI.motivation: To understand how nanoconfinement affects methane hydrate nucleation, which is poorly understood due to the complex interplay between geometric restriction and molecular ordering.
AI.method: Molecular dynamics simulations of water-methane systems confined between silica planar slit pores (1–5 nm width) at temperatures of 250–295 K, analyzed using three-dimensional radial distribution functions and projected two-dimensional correlations.
AI.result: 3D radial distribution functions show suppressed hydrate-like ordering at strong confinement (<2 nm), indicating frustrated nucleation. 2D projected correlations reveal pronounced in-plane structural organization, demonstrating confinement-induced reduction in the dimensionality of molecular order.
AI.conclusion: Strong nanoconfinement frustrates methane hydrate nucleation by suppressing 3D ordering, while promoting in-plane structural organization due to reduced dimensionality, highlighting the critical role of pore size in controlling hydrate formation.

title: Biquadratic exchange coupling effect on the magnetic properties of (Fe/Ti) multilayers
summary: This work explores the static and dynamic magnetic properties of weakly antiferromagnetically coupled Fe/Ti superlattices, emphasizing the link between magnetic behavior and structural characteristics. HRTEM and XRD analyses confirm alternating Fe and Ti layers with rough interfaces, especially in upper layers. Magnetic measurements reveal two-step hysteresis loops and a temperature and thickness-dependent interlayer exchange coupling (IEC). A macrospin model incorporating bilinear and biquadratic coupling reproduces the experimental data and supports a phase diagram analysis identifying non-collinear configurations. The results underscore the impact of structural imperfections and highlight the crucial role of biquadratic exchange in Fe/Ti/Fe multilayers.

AI.tldr: The paper studies Fe/Ti superlattices with weak antiferromagnetic coupling, using structural analysis and magnetic measurements to reveal two-step hysteresis loops and temperature/thickness-dependent interlayer exchange coupling. A macrospin model with bilinear and biquadratic coupling reproduces experiments and identifies non-collinear magnetic configurations.
AI.motivation: To explore the link between magnetic behavior (static and dynamic) and structural characteristics in weakly antiferromagnetically coupled Fe/Ti superlattices, particularly the role of structural imperfections and biquadratic exchange.
AI.method: HRTEM and XRD for structural characterization; magnetic measurements for hysteresis loops; macrospin model incorporating bilinear and biquadratic coupling; phase diagram analysis.
AI.result: Two-step hysteresis loops observed; interlayer exchange coupling depends on temperature and thickness; rough interfaces present especially in upper layers; macrospin model with biquadratic coupling reproduces data; non-collinear configurations identified.
AI.conclusion: Structural imperfections significantly impact magnetic behavior; biquadratic exchange plays a crucial role in Fe/Ti/Fe multilayers.

title: Tunable Dual-Type Weyl Points in Dirac-Weyl Semimetal CaAgBi
summary: Dirac-Weyl semimetals host both Dirac and Weyl fermions and the exploration of material candidates with tunable topological properties is essential to realize topological spintronic devices. In this work, we propose CaAgBi as a Dirac-Weyl semimetal with tunable type-I and type-II Weyl points based on first-principle calculations. In addition to the three pairs of Dirac points located along the rotational axis as previously reported, our calculations reveal 18 additional pairs of dual-type Weyl points distributed across three distinct planes: type-I in the $k_z=0$ plane and type-II in the $k_z= \pm 0.0698\,\frac{2π}{c}$ planes. The topological features are further confirmed through chirality of the Weyl points as well as the existence of surface Fermi arcs. Moreover, we find that the position and annihilation of Dirac and Weyl points are tunable by the alloy engineering and external strains. The alloy engineering is employed to modulate the positions of Weyl points, revealing different annihilation concentrations for type-I and type-II Weyl points, potentially offering novel experimental strategies for Weyl point manipulation. Under tensile biaxial strain, the Weyl points in the $k_{z}=0$ plane annihilate along the $Γ$--$\mathrm{M}$ path at $2.1\%$ strain, whereas the Weyl points in the $k_{z}\neq 0$ planes remain robust within $6\%$ strain. This work provides a versatile platform for manipulating Dirac/Weyl interactions, with spin-orbit coupling (SOC) driven alloy control and strain-selective engineering opening avenues for topological electronics.

AI.tldr: CaAgBi is identified as a Dirac-Weyl semimetal with 18 additional dual-type Weyl points beyond known Dirac points; its topological properties are tunable via alloy engineering and external strain, offering a platform for topological electronics.
AI.motivation: To explore material candidates with tunable topological properties for realizing topological spintronic devices, specifically focusing on Dirac-Weyl semimetals that host both Dirac and Weyl fermions.
AI.method: First-principle calculations (DFT) to study electronic structure; chirality analysis for Weyl point identification; alloy engineering and external biaxial strain to modulate Weyl/Dirac point positions and annihilation.
AI.result: Discovered 18 additional pairs of dual-type Weyl points (type-I in k_z=0 plane, type-II in k_z=±0.0698·2π/c planes) beyond 3 known Dirac pairs; type-I Weyl points annihilate at 2.1% tensile biaxial strain along Γ-M, while type-II persist up to 6%; alloy engineering shows different annihilation concentrations for type-I vs type-II.
AI.conclusion: CaAgBi is a versatile platform for manipulating Dirac/Weyl interactions, with SOC-driven alloy control and strain-selective engineering providing new strategies for topological electronics.

title: N-Graphdiyne as a Tunable Platform for Stabilizing Light Metals toward High-Capacity Reversible Hydrogen Storage
summary: Hydrogen (H2) is a promising carbon-neutral energy carrier. However, its deployment is limited by the lack of lightweight, reversible storage media that operate under practical conditions. Here, we establish nitrogen-doped graphdiyne (N-GDY) as a programmable two-dimensional platform for stabilizing dispersed light-metal dopants and enabling high-capacity physisorption of molecular H2. The computational package involves density functional theory (DFT) combined with ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and Langmuir-based statistical thermodynamic modeling. The results revealed that N-sites of N-GDY bind up to five Li, Na, K, and Ca atoms per primitive cell with binding energies of -2.27, -1.57, -1.80, and -2.13 eV, respectively, exceeding their respective bulk cohesive energies. AIMD simulations at 400 K further confirm the structural robustness of the decorated frameworks and the absence of metal aggregation. The polarised metal centres activate reversible H2 adsorption through electrostatic and dispersion interactions, with average adsorption energies falling within the optimal window (-0.15 to -0.35 eV per H2). Sequential adsorption analysis reveals uptake of up to 25 H2 molecules per primitive cell, achieving intrinsic gravimetric capacities of 13.08, 10.82, 9.23, and 9.15 wt% for Li-, Na-, K-, and Ca-functionalized systems, respectively. Thermodynamic analysis indicates favorable adsorption-desorption behavior under near-ambient conditions, with Li- and Ca-functionalized systems exceeding the 6.5 wt% U.S. Department of Energy's ultimate system-level target when considering intrinsic material capacity. These results identify N-GDY as a chemically tunable scaffold for dispersing lightweight metals and provide a mechanistic design strategy for achieving high-capacity, reversible hydrogen storage in porous two-dimensional materials.

AI.tldr: Nitrogen-doped graphdiyne (N-GDY) is established as a programmable 2D platform for stabilizing dispersed light-metal dopants (Li, Na, K, Ca), enabling high-capacity reversible H₂ physisorption. DFT, AIMD, and Langmuir modeling show up to 25 H₂ molecules per primitive cell, achieving gravimetric capacities up to 13.08 wt% (Li-system), with Li and Ca systems exceeding the DOE 6.5 wt% target under near-ambient conditions.
AI.motivation: Hydrogen is a promising carbon-neutral energy carrier but its deployment is limited by the lack of lightweight, reversible storage media that operate under practical conditions.
AI.method: Density functional theory (DFT) combined with ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and Langmuir-based statistical thermodynamic modeling.
AI.result: N-sites of N-GDY bind up to five Li, Na, K, and Ca atoms per primitive cell with binding energies of -2.27, -1.57, -1.80, and -2.13 eV, exceeding bulk cohesive energies. AIMD at 400 K confirms structural robustness. Up to 25 H₂ molecules per primitive cell, achieving 13.08, 10.82, 9.23, and 9.15 wt% for Li-, Na-, K-, and Ca-systems. Li and Ca systems exceed DOE 6.5 wt% target.
AI.conclusion: N-GDY is a chemically tunable scaffold for dispersing lightweight metals, providing a mechanistic design strategy for achieving high-capacity, reversible hydrogen storage in porous 2D materials.

title: Agentic Design of Compositional Descriptors via Autoresearch for Materials Science Applications
summary: Autoresearch offers a flexible paradigm for automating scientific tasks, in which an AI agent proposes, implements, evaluates, and refines candidate solutions against a quantitative objective. Here, we use composition-based materials-property prediction to test whether such agents can perform a task beyond model selection and hyperparameter optimization: the design of input descriptors. We introduce Automat, an autoresearch framework where a coding agent based on a large language model generates composition-only descriptors for chemical compounds and evaluates them using a random forest workflow. The agent is restricted to information derivable from chemical formulas and iteratively proposes, implements, and tests chemically motivated descriptor strategies. We apply Automat, with OpenAI Codex using GPT-5.5 as the coding agent, to the prediction of experimental band gaps in inorganic materials and Curie temperatures in ferromagnetic compounds. In both tasks, Automat improves over fractional-composition, Magpie, and combined fractional-composition/Magpie baselines, while producing descriptor families that are chemically interpretable. These results provide a demonstration that autoresearch agents can generate competitive, task-specific materials descriptors without manual feature engineering during the run. They also reveal current limitations, including descriptor redundancy, sensitivity to greedy feature expansion, and the need for explicit complexity control, descriptor pruning, and more sophisticated search strategies.

AI.tldr: Automat, an autoresearch framework using LLM-driven coding agents, generates composition-only descriptors for materials property prediction, outperforming baselines on band gap and Curie temperature prediction while producing chemically interpretable features.
AI.motivation: To test whether AI autoresearch agents can perform beyond model selection/hyperparameter optimization—specifically, the design of input descriptors for materials-property prediction—and to explore automated, chemically motivated feature engineering without manual intervention.
AI.method: Automat framework: an LLM-based coding agent (OpenAI Codex with GPT-5.5) iteratively proposes, implements, and evaluates composition-only descriptors for chemical compounds using a random forest workflow, restricted to information derivable from chemical formulas.
AI.result: Automat outperformed fractional-composition, Magpie, and combined baselines on experimental band gap and Curie temperature prediction; produced chemically interpretable descriptor families; revealed limitations such as descriptor redundancy, sensitivity to greedy feature expansion, and need for complexity control and pruning.
AI.conclusion: Autoresearch agents can generate competitive, task-specific materials descriptors without manual feature engineering, but current limitations require explicit complexity control, descriptor pruning, and more sophisticated search strategies for broader applicability.

title: Telecom-Wavelength-Compatible Quantum Information Transcription Using Nitrogen-Vacancy Centers
summary: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a leading platform for solid-state quantum sensing and quantum information processing. While most optical studies rely on the visible fluorescence associated with the triplet transitions, the infrared singlet transition near $1042$ nm, which is typically considered dark within the singlet manifold of the NV optical cycle, provides an alternative optical channel. Here, we report wavelength-resolved optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) measurements of this infrared emission. We directly observe ODMR contrast in the $1042$ nm emission and analyze its dependence on the magnetic field. The field-dependent spectral dispersion of the ODMR signal demonstrates that the spin-state information encoded in the NV center is transcribed to the infrared singlet emission through the spin-selective intersystem crossing, in close analogy to the visible fluorescence readout. These results establish infrared ODMR as a high-fidelity optical readout pathway. Crucially, by extending spin-state transcription directly into the $1300-1600$ nm range, this work demonstrates a direct, conversion-free interface between diamond spin-qubits and standard telecommunication infrastructure, bypassing the efficiency bottlenecks of active frequency conversion and benefiting from the already well-developed technologies in this range of the electromagnetic spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates infrared optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) at 1042 nm of NV centers in diamond, showing spin-state information is transcribed to the infrared singlet emission. It establishes a direct interface between diamond spin-qubits and telecom wavelengths (1300-1600 nm), avoiding the need for active frequency conversion.
AI.motivation: To explore the infrared singlet transition (1042 nm) of NV centers as an alternative optical readout channel beyond the conventional visible fluorescence, and to enable direct coupling to telecommunication infrastructure without efficiency losses from frequency conversion.
AI.method: Wavelength-resolved ODMR measurements of the infrared emission (1042 nm) from NV centers, analyzing the field-dependent spectral dispersion and contrast of the ODMR signal to verify spin-state transcription via spin-selective intersystem crossing.
AI.result: Direct observation of ODMR contrast in the 1042 nm emission; field-dependent spectral dispersion confirms that spin-state information is transcribed from the NV center to the infrared singlet emission through spin-selective intersystem crossing, analogous to visible fluorescence readout.
AI.conclusion: Infrared ODMR provides a high-fidelity optical readout pathway, and by extending spin-state transcription into the 1300-1600 nm telecom range, this work demonstrates a direct, conversion-free interface between diamond spin-qubits and standard telecommunication infrastructure.

title: Thermal expansion of FeWO$_4$ (Ferberite) and FeWO$_4$:Fe$_2$WO$_6$ (7:1): a comparative X-ray and neutron diffraction study
summary: The thermal expansion of natural FeWO$_4$ (ferberite) and synthetic FeWO$_4$:Fe$_2$WO$_6$ (7:1) was investigated over the 2-1123 K temperature range combining single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction together with neutron powder diffraction. High-precision lattice parameters were obtained for both samples. The temperature dependence of the unit-cell volume was analysed using physically based thermodynamic models, including the Kroll and Berman approaches as implemented in EoSFit7. All datasets are well reproduced within their respective temperature intervals. However, significant differences are observed between the behavior of ferberite and FeWO$_4$:Fe$_2$WO$_6$, which has a \~40% smaller thermal expansion coefficient and a reduced reference volume. Possible origins, including microstructural and phase-coexistence effects, are discussed. The results provide a comprehensive description of the thermal expansion behavior of FeWO$_4$ across a wide temperature range.

AI.tldr: This study investigates the thermal expansion of natural ferberite (FeWO₄) and synthetic FeWO₄:Fe₂WO₆ (7:1) from 2-1123 K using X-ray and neutron diffraction, finding that the synthetic sample has ~40% lower thermal expansion and smaller reference volume, with potential microstructural causes discussed.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive, high-precision description of the thermal expansion behavior of FeWO₄ across an exceptionally wide temperature range (2-1123 K), and to understand differences between natural and synthetic variants.
AI.method: Combined single-crystal X-ray diffraction, powder X-ray diffraction, and neutron powder diffraction from 2-1123 K; thermodynamic modeling using Kroll and Berman approaches in EoSFit7.
AI.result: High-precision lattice parameters obtained for both samples; synthetic FeWO₄:Fe₂WO₆ exhibits ~40% smaller thermal expansion coefficient and reduced reference volume compared to natural ferberite.
AI.conclusion: All datasets are well reproduced by the thermodynamic models; differences between samples likely arise from microstructural and phase-coexistence effects, providing a comprehensive thermal expansion description for FeWO₄.

title: Melting Behavior and Phase Stability of CaO from Neural Network Potentials: a Molecular Dynamics Study
summary: We investigate the melting behavior of calcium oxide (CaO) under extreme conditions, a problem that remains poorly constrained due to experimental limitations despite its relevance for geophysical and technological applications. We develop a Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (MLIP) for CaO with PANNA 2.0 and the LATTE descriptor, training it on a dataset of $\sim$12,000 configurations including solid, liquid, interfacial, and void-containing structures, extracted from ab-initio molecular dynamics data employing PBEsol exchange-correlation functional. We perform large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to compute the melting temperature at ambient pressure using both the void-nucleated melting (VNM) and two-phase coexistence (TPC) methods, obtaining $T_m=3055\pm11$ K and $T_m=2847\pm15$ K, respectively.\\ We calculate an enthalpy of fusion of $ΔH_f\sim73$ kJ/mol, in agreement with thermodynamic assessments and ab initio calculations. We also reproduce the thermal expansion and obtain a volume increase of $\sim$29% at Tm, consistent with the corresponding decrease in density extracted from spatially resolved number density profiles. Finally, we calculate the high-pressure melting curve of CaO up to 20 GPa, providing one of the very few computational determinations of this quantity to date. The results confirm that the overheating ratio $η$ is not constant under pressure, increasing from 17% at ambient pressure to 24% at 20 GPa, confirming previous findings and ruling out the assumption of a fixed overheating ratio. Our results establish MLIP-based simulations as a robust and efficient framework for investigating phase stability in ionic oxides and provide new insight into the melting behavior of CaO under extreme conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (MLIP) for CaO to study its melting behavior under extreme conditions. The authors compute melting temperatures at ambient pressure using two methods (VNM: 3055±11 K, TPC: 2847±15 K), enthalpy of fusion (~73 kJ/mol), thermal expansion, and the high-pressure melting curve up to 20 GPa. They find the overheating ratio increases from 17% to 24% under pressure, ruling out a fixed ratio assumption.
AI.motivation: The melting behavior of CaO under extreme conditions remains poorly constrained due to experimental limitations, despite its relevance for geophysical (e.g., Earth's mantle) and technological applications.
AI.method: The authors develop a Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (MLIP) for CaO using PANNA 2.0 and the LATTE descriptor, trained on ~12,000 configurations from ab-initio molecular dynamics (PBEsol functional). They perform large-scale MD simulations using void-nucleated melting (VNM) and two-phase coexistence (TPC) methods.
AI.result: Melting temperatures: Tm=3055±11 K (VNM) and Tm=2847±15 K (TPC) at ambient pressure. Enthalpy of fusion ~73 kJ/mol. Volume increase ~29% at Tm. High-pressure melting curve computed up to 20 GPa. Overheating ratio increases from 17% (ambient) to 24% (20 GPa).
AI.conclusion: MLIP-based simulations provide a robust and efficient framework for studying phase stability in ionic oxides. The overheating ratio is not constant under pressure, ruling out the fixed overheating ratio assumption and providing new insight into CaO melting under extreme conditions.

title: Generative reconstruction of 2D and 3D polycrystalline microstructures using symmetrized hyperspherical harmonics
summary:
Establishing structure-property linkages in polycrystalline materials requires representative two- (2D) and three- (3D) dimensional microstructural inputs for full-field simulations. A core objective of microstructure characterization and reconstruction is the generative synthesis of 2D and 3D microstructures that reflect a target statistical ensemble using limited 2D data as a reference. This work introduces an orientation-based differentiable microstructure characterization and reconstruction framework, implemented in MCRpy, to perform reconstructions of voxelized images. Unit quaternions in combination with symmetrized hyperspherical harmonics are utilized to derive a continuous, symmetry-invariant representation of crystallographic orientations to overcome the numerical singularities and discontinuities associated with traditional Euler-based methods.
  The descriptor-based reconstructions are driven by a set combining two-point spatial correlations, a novel hybrid three-point variogram, and a mean variation regularizer to capture both global texture and local interfacial topology. The framework's efficiency is demonstrated by reconstructing 3D realizations from 2D orientation data of an aluminum alloy after thermo-mechanical processing, successfully recovering both morphological features and crystallographic distribution. Systematic benchmarking indicates that second-order gradient-based optimization, utilizing the L-BFGS-B algorithm, effectively navigates the complex loss landscape to generate high-fidelity realizations with minimal residuals. This methodology provides a versatile, open-source framework for the digital synthesis of polycrystalline representative volume elements to facilitate the rapid development of microstructure-informed materials design workflows.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an orientation-based differentiable microstructure characterization and reconstruction framework (MCRpy) that uses unit quaternions, symmetrized hyperspherical harmonics, and a hybrid set of descriptors (two-point correlations, three-point variogram, mean variation regularizer) to reconstruct 3D polycrystalline microstructures from limited 2D orientation data, demonstrated on an aluminum alloy with high fidelity using L-BFGS-B optimization.
AI.motivation: Establishing structure-property linkages in polycrystalline materials requires representative 2D/3D microstructural inputs for full-field simulations, but generating such 3D data from limited 2D references remains challenging, especially due to numerical singularities and discontinuities in traditional Euler-based orientation representations.
AI.method: An orientation-based differentiable microstructure characterization and reconstruction framework (MCRpy) using: (1) unit quaternions with symmetrized hyperspherical harmonics for continuous, symmetry-invariant orientation representation; (2) descriptor-based reconstruction driven by two-point spatial correlations, a novel hybrid three-point variogram, and a mean variation regularizer; (3) L-BFGS-B second-order gradient-based optimization.
AI.result: Successfully reconstructed 3D microstructural realizations from 2D orientation data of a thermo-mechanically processed aluminum alloy, recovering both morphological features and crystallographic distributions with minimal residuals via systematic benchmarking.
AI.conclusion: The methodology provides a versatile, open-source framework for digital synthesis of polycrystalline representative volume elements, facilitating rapid development of microstructure-informed materials design workflows.

title: The Emergence of Photonic Crystalline Order and Time-Series Dynamics in NaCl Droplet Deposition
summary: Crystallization during droplet evaporation gives rise to complex, self-organized structures, yet the mechanisms underlying the emergence of ordered functional phases remain poorly understood. In this study, we present a comprehensive, multi-scale investigation into the crystallization dynamics of NaCl during droplet evaporation on a germanium (001) substrate, relevant for its IR applications. Through systematic microscopic characterization, we identify the formation of diverse microstructures, including 1D photonic crystal nanostructures formed within hybrid crystal-glass photonic system. To enable quantitative comparison across experimental conditions, we introduce the NaCl equivalent height as a unified metric to describe and classify the evolution of crystalline morphology. Our results reveal that diffusion anisotropy, rather than growth kinetics, primarily governs the maximal attainable structure size. Quantitative thin film interference analysis demonstrates the presence of discrete thickness layers in the film. Controlled evaporation experiments yield homogeneous crystallization patterns across the entire droplet area, facilitating the emergence of ordered photonic structures. Time-series dynamics analysis of height profiles uncovered the spatiotemporal evolution of the crystallization front, providing insights into the details of underlying physical mechanisms. Together, these results establish a robust experimental framework for understanding and predicting crystallization behavior in evaporating droplets, with potential applications in materials synthesis, photonics, and microscale pattern formation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates NaCl crystallization dynamics during droplet evaporation on a germanium substrate, revealing diffusion anisotropy as the primary factor governing structure size, and demonstrating ordered photonic structures through controlled evaporation.
AI.motivation: The mechanisms underlying the emergence of ordered functional phases during droplet evaporation crystallization remain poorly understood, motivating a comprehensive multi-scale investigation.
AI.method: Multi-scale microscopic characterization, NaCl equivalent height as a unified metric, quantitative thin film interference analysis, controlled evaporation experiments, and time-series dynamics analysis of height profiles.
AI.result: Diffusion anisotropy primarily governs maximal structure size; discrete thickness layers identified via thin film interference; homogeneous crystallization patterns achieved under controlled evaporation; spatiotemporal evolution of crystallization front characterized.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a robust experimental framework for understanding and predicting crystallization behavior in evaporating droplets, with applications in materials synthesis, photonics, and microscale pattern formation.

title: Limitations of Debye-Waller lattice temperature extraction under electronic excitation
summary: Ultrafast diffraction is the cutting-edge technique to extract the atomic temperature at femtosecond timescales, and further related quantities - in particular, electron-phonon coupling strength at elevated electronic temperatures. The present work demonstrates limitations of such an analysis, emphasizing the importance of careful evaluation of the evolution of the Debye temperature. It is shown that, due to the sensitivity of the Debye-Waller analysis to this parameter, neglecting its changes under electronic excitation may lead to significant deviations of the atomic temperature extracted from its true values.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that neglecting changes in Debye temperature under electronic excitation can significantly distort atomic temperature measurements from ultrafast diffraction, affecting derived electron-phonon coupling strengths.
AI.motivation: Ultrafast diffraction is used to extract atomic temperature at femtosecond timescales and related quantities like electron-phonon coupling strength. The authors aim to show limitations of this analysis and emphasize the importance of evaluating the evolution of the Debye temperature.
AI.method: The authors analyze the sensitivity of the Debye-Waller analysis to the Debye temperature parameter. They demonstrate how neglecting changes in Debye temperature under electronic excitation affects the accuracy of extracted atomic temperatures.
AI.result: Due to the sensitivity of the Debye-Waller analysis to the Debye temperature, neglecting its changes under electronic excitation leads to significant deviations of the extracted atomic temperature from its true values.
AI.conclusion: Careful evaluation of the evolution of the Debye temperature is essential for accurate atomic temperature extraction via ultrafast diffraction, and failure to do so yields unreliable electron-phonon coupling strength measurements.
